Inglewood, California
  October 17, 2023

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  October 17, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Faulk, Morales; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Jeffery Lewis  Acting City Attorney/Acting General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  October 12, 2023, in the amount of $6,068,479.02, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members Gray,
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman / Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

101  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – IT’S YOUR PARTY FLORAL & EVENT DESIGN
  (IT’S YOUR PARTY). Staff report dated October 17, 2023, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members authorize the payment of an outstanding invoice
  submitted by It’s Your Party Floral & Event Design (It’s Your Party), for two (2) Keys to
  the City.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $1,870. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
 October 17, 2023

178  BLANKET PURCHASE ORDER AUTHORIZED – DOOLEY ENTERPRISES, INC.
  Staff report dated October 17, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members authorize issuance of a blanket purchase order to Dooley Enterprises,
  Inc., for the purchase of practice and duty ammunition.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize issuance in a total amount not to exceed
  $138,318.40. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  RESOLUTION NO. 24-05 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE 2023-2024 FISCAL YEAR
  BUDGET. Staff report dated October 17, 2023, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2023-2024
  Budget to include Fiscal Year 2021 Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI) grant funds, in
  the amount of $69,555, from the previous fiscal year.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 24-05 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2023-2024 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  CHIEF OF POLICE RECOMMENDATIONS ACCEPTED AND APPROVED –
  EXPENDITURE OF FISCAL YEAR 2023 JAG FUNDS - AUTHORIZED. Staff report
  dated October 17, 2023, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  accept and approve the recommendation of the Chief of Police pertaining to the expenditure
  of Fiscal Year 2023 Justice Assistance Grant funds.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Accept and approve recommendation of the Chief of
  Police; 2) Receive and file this report pertaining to the United States Department of Justice
  (USDOJ) Fiscal Year 2023 Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG); 3) Approve
  Certifications and Assurances required for acceptance of Fiscal Year 2023 JAG funds; and
  4) Authorize the expenditure of Fiscal Year 2023 JAG funds in the amount of $55,971 for
  the approved recommendation. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  URBAN FOREST MANAGEMENT PLAN ADOPTED – MANAGING AND
  MAINTENANCE OF CITY TREES. Staff report dated October 17, 2023, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt the Urban Forest Management
  Plan (Plan), establishing the plan as a comprehensive guide for managing and maintaining
  City Trees (urban forest), ensuring their preservation and sustainable growth.
  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented a Staff Report dated October 17, 2023, and introduced
  Louis Atwell, Public Works Director.

  Louis Atwell, Public Works Director, presented a brief introduction regarding the Urban
  Forest Management Plan and introduced the presenter.

  Timothy Crothers, West Coast Arborist Representative, presented an oral report regarding
  the Urban Forest Management Plan which included; current state of the City of Inglewood
  Urban Forest, the Vision, specific goals, and how the visions were realized in the Urban
  Forest Management Plan.

  2
 October 17, 2023

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby adopt the Urban Forest Management Plan. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson congratulated Council
  Member Padilla on the 100th Year Celebration of Fairview Heights that she attended.  She
  stated that Council Member Padilla always arranges significant events for the  residents  of
  District 2, and she knows the residents are happy. She wished Destinee, a Staff Assistant  in
  the City Clerk’s Office, a Happy 31st Birthday.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) spoke concerning residents being required to pay for permits to
  park. He complained that the attendees take up all the parking when there is a game. He
  stated that Parking Enforcement couldn't cite all unauthorized cars because they have to
  bring it up on their computer. He suggested that Parking Enforcement obtain a handheld
  device to determine which cars belong. He mentioned having evening Council Meetings.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) questioned the time the City has worked with West Coast
  Arborist and whether it went out for bid. She stated that she was familiar with the company; they
  are tree doctors well-known in the City and County of Los Angeles.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) cited scriptures from the Bible that he stood by. He stated that
  he wanted the Council to know that he has opened six locations since March for his youth
  ministry, and some investors invested six million dollars because they knew him. He
  mentioned that his products were available at Best Buy, Walmart, and Target and that
  athletic companies use his mouth guards. Additionally, he mentioned wrong information given
  to the building owner by city employees and requested an investigation into a  property
  because it was messed up before his arrival. He also requested a meeting with  the Mayor and
  Council Member Morales and stated that he had left messages for a long time. Finally, he
  addressed the number of years he had known the mayor and stated that  he never left the vision
  that was given to him by God.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in honor of Mayor of Carson Lula Davis's grandson, and Jimmy Kinoshita,
  Council Member Morales' father-in-law, at the hour of 2:38 p.m.

  Approved this 12th day of December, 2023.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
